meta_scope: This assigns the given scope to all text within this context, including the patterns that push the context onto the stack and pop it off.
meta_content_scope: As above, but does not apply to the text that triggers the context.

clear_scopes: … It can be an integer.

Meta patterns must be listed first in the context, before any match or include patterns — with no stated consequence when they are not.
push: … an inline, anonymous context.
The main context uses a match pattern that pushes two contexts on the stack, with the rightmost context in the list becoming the topmost context on the stack.
pop: … An integer greater than zero will pop the corresponding number of contexts.
set: … Any match will receive the meta_scope of the context being popped and the context being pushed.
A variation: a set of several contexts at once.
For push, embed and branch actions, the pop treats the match as if it were a lookahead, which means the match will not receive the meta_scope of the contexts that are popped.
The lookahead sentence names push, embed and branch and not set, whose own entry says the trigger receives the popped context's meta_scope.
A variation: the same for a pop: N + branch:, which the lookahead sentence does name.
embed: … it pops out of any number of nested contexts as soon as the escape pattern is found.
escape: … Any backreferences in this pattern will refer to capture groups in the match regex.
embed_scope: A scope assigned to all text matched after the match and before the escape. escape_captures: … Use capture group 0 to apply a scope to the entire escape match.
A variation: escape_captures on a group other than 0.
Using pop with another action: the reference's own pop: 1 + embed: example.
A variation: an embed inside an embed, and which escape closes which.
branch: Accepts the names of two or more contexts, which are attempted in order.
If a fail action is encountered, the highlighting of the file will be restarted at the character where the branch occurred, and the next context will be attempted.
A variation: three alternatives, the first two of which fail.
fail: … If a fail action specifies a branch_point that was never pushed on the stack … it will have no effect.

captures: A mapping of numbers to scope, assigning scopes to captured portions of the match regex — here nested groups.

with_prototype … will be always be inserted into every referenced context irrespective of their meta_include_prototype key.

A variation: a with_prototype is the pushing rule's, so it stops where that context is popped.

A variation: a variable inside an escape regex.
A syntax using inheritance will inherit the variables and contexts values from its parent syntax.
Contexts with the same name will override contexts from the parent syntax.
meta_prepend: true — all of the patterns in the extending syntax will be inserted before those in the parent syntax.
meta_append: true — … inserted after to any existing rules from a context with the same name in an ancestor syntax definition.
Thus, an extending syntax may change a variable from a parent syntax, and all usage of the variable in the parent contexts will use the overridden value.
A variation: a context the child adds beside the ones it inherits.
The parent syntaxes will be processed in order, from top to bottom, and must be derived from the same base.

There are no enforced limits on extending, other than that all syntaxes must share the same version.
